prompts: Our support assistant's conversations are already saved in Weave. I can't read every exchange. I want it to pick out the ones where the customer sounds confused or annoyed so my team can review them. Where would I set that up, and where would I see the matches? Explain without assuming I know the product's terminology.
expected_behavior: Translate the request into an agent Signal that tags user frustration. The User Frustration preset is sufficient; a custom tag with an equivalent detection definition is also valid. Explain the Agents > Signals creation path and where scored or tagged turns appear for inspection. Define unfamiliar terms briefly. Do not require coding, a particular model, a custom signal when the preset suffices, or unrelated setup steps because traces already exist.

assertions.description: Identifies the User Frustration tag Signal, or an equivalent custom tag definition, as a way to flag confused or annoyed customers for review.
Gives an actionable setup path through the project's Agents > Signals view and creates or enables the relevant preset or custom signal.
Explains that matching or scored turns can be inspected in the Signals table, rather than claiming the feature automatically rewrites the agent's replies.

prompts: We already trace our Python agent and have a human-review Signal. A teammate suggested @weave.op(tracing_sample_rate=0.1) to make that Signal inspect about one in ten turns while keeping all the traces. Is that the right control? If not, what should we change?
expected_behavior: Correct the use of a real API in the wrong layer. tracing_sample_rate on an Op controls collection of that Op's traces; it is not the Signal scoring sample rate and sampled-out Op calls do not send trace data. Preserve the existing agent tracing and set the Signal's Advanced sample rate to 0.1 (10%) for matching turns. Do not promise exactly every tenth turn or imply changing an Op decorator alone controls all agent-turn instrumentation.

assertions.description: Distinguishes the Op's tracing_sample_rate, which controls trace collection for Op calls, from the Signal's scoring sample rate.
Explains that the proposed Op sampling setting can omit trace data, so it does not satisfy the goal of keeping all traces while reducing only Signal scoring.
Recommends setting the Signal's Advanced sample rate to 0.1 or 10% of matching turns, leaving the existing trace collection intact.

prompts: Our new instrumentation shows conversations and turns in Weave's Agents view. I found the 'Set up custom monitors' guide, which talks about choosing operations on the Monitors page. We want a custom tag for answers needing human review. Can I follow that guide unchanged, or what setup should I use for these agent turns?
expected_behavior: Use the introductory workflow warning rather than merging old and new instructions. The custom-monitors guide is a previous approach; new agent-turn implementations should use Agents > Signals. Explain creating a Custom Signal with a tag name and a behavioral definition. It is acceptable to mention that some underlying SDK objects are still named Monitor; do not claim all Monitor classes or existing legacy workflows are invalid.

assertions.description: Recognizes that the custom-monitors guide describes the previous workflow and directs this new agent-turn implementation to Signals under Agents.
Provides the Agents > Signals > New signal or Create your first signal > Custom Signal path for the requested tag.
Describes a tag name and a definition of which answers need review, instead of transferring legacy Calls operation-selection instructions unchanged.

prompts: We're starting a hand-written Python support agent on Weave's multi-tenant cloud. I need three connected pieces: inspect its multi-turn conversations and tool calls, rerun a fixed set of regression questions when we change it, and send completed live answers to our own HTTP policy-scoring endpoint. Give me a compact setup outline. What remote-scoring prerequisites must be in place before Weave can call that endpoint, and does that scoring finish before the user receives the answer?
expected_behavior: Connect three documented workflows without treating them as one automatic pipeline: initialize and instrument the custom agent with grouped conversations, per-exchange turns and LLM/tool spans; use weave.Evaluation with fixed examples and scorers for repeatable checks; create a remote-scorer Signal for completed live turns. For multi-tenant cloud, remote scoring must be enabled by an organization or billing admin and the endpoint host allowed; use an allowed HTTPS endpoint. Explain that scoring is asynchronous after a turn completes, so it is not a synchronous pre-response guardrail. No full runnable integration, authentication variant, environment-variable inventory, exact retry schedule, or numerical truth guarantee is required.

assertions.description: Places weave.init with a team/project before the custom agent tracing APIs.
Explains a stable conversation grouping with a turn for each exchange and LLM/tool spans for the work inside a turn.
Uses weave.Evaluation with fixed example data and scoring functions, run against the agent or application function, for repeatable regression checks.
Uses a remote-scorer Signal to send completed live agent turns to the team's HTTP endpoint, distinct from the fixed-dataset evaluation.
States the multi-tenant prerequisites: an organization or billing admin enables remote scoring and allows the HTTPS scorer endpoint's host.
Explains that remote Signal scoring is asynchronous after the turn completes, not a documented synchronous gate that must finish before the answer is returned.

prompts: I'm instrumenting a Python agent by hand. How can I attach env='staging' to just one turn in its trace?
Correction: this deployment is TypeScript, and I want env='production' on every span in the conversation. Show the minimal setup for that. Do I have to repeat the metadata on each LLM and tool span?
expected_behavior: Apply the user's correction to both language and scope. Use TypeScript import/setup with awaited weave.init and weave.startConversation({attributes: {env: 'production'}}), or a semantically equivalent documented TypeScript example. Explain that conversation attributes are stamped on every emitted turn, LLM, tool and sub-agent span; no repetition on each child is needed for this shared value. Do not continue prescribing Python-only set_attributes for one staging turn. The custom key env is sufficient; no unrelated reserved-prefix lecture or complete agent implementation is mandatory.

assertions.description: Uses the corrected TypeScript context for the final setup rather than continuing with Python-only calls.
Shows awaited weave.init before starting the TypeScript conversation.
Passes env: 'production' through the attributes option of weave.startConversation, or the equivalent documented conversation-level API.
Explains that the shared conversation attributes propagate to emitted child spans, so the user need not repeat env on each LLM or tool span.

prompts: I'm inside a nested Python helper called by my instrumented agent. I saw weave.get_current_conversation() in a reference and want to use it instead of passing the conversation object through every function. Is it a real documented API, what does it return, and what happens when no conversation is active? Show a small usage example.
expected_behavior: Answer the documented question directly. weave.get_current_conversation() retrieves the active Conversation from context and returns None if none is active. A small helper can retrieve it and check for None; no mandatory clarification or refusal is warranted. Do not substitute get_current_session as the preferred API, invent a required argument, claim it starts a conversation, or claim the example was executed against Weave. The agent may qualify the answer as applying to the saved documentation snapshot.

assertions.description: Confirms and uses the documented no-argument weave.get_current_conversation() API to retrieve the currently active conversation.
States that the return value is the active Conversation or None when no conversation is active.
Provides a small Python example retrieving the active conversation inside a helper, without inventing required arguments or starting a new conversation merely to retrieve the existing one.
